claims.text: MOA: bactericidal; inhibits phosphoenolpyruvate synthetase, blocking peptidoglycan (cell wall) synth; unrelated to other abx classes.
claims.quote: Fosfomycin is a novel class of antibiotic with a chemical structure unrelated to other known antibiotics. It is a bactericidal medication that disrupts cell wall synthesis by inhibiting phosphoenolpyruvate synthetase and thus interferes with the production of peptidoglycan.

claims.text: Treats: gram (+) and gram (-) incl MRSA, VRE and ESBL-producing or FQ-resistant E. coli; PO only for uncomp (lower) UTI from E. coli or enterococci.
claims.quote: Fosfomycin has activity against both gram-positive and gram-negative organisms, including some antibiotic-resistant organisms such as Staphylococcus aureus, including methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) Enterococcus species, including vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) Escherichia coli, including extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)–producing and fluoroquinolone-resistant E. coli Oral fosfomycin should be used only for uncomplicated (ie, lower) urinary tract infections caused by E. coli or enterococci.

claims.text: Know: ↓PO bioavailability, so ⍉for pyelonephritis; urine levels stay therapeutic > 24 h.
claims.quote: Oral bioavailability of the fosfomycin tromethamine salt is low (about 40%), and, consequently, serum levels are low relative to the minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs). For this reason, fosfomycin is used to treat uncomplicated lower urinary tract infections, not pyelonephritis. Fosfomycin does not bind to plasma proteins and distributes widely into tissues. Fosfomycin is excreted in urine mainly by glomerular filtration without biotransformation. After oral dosing, urinary levels exceed the MICs of susceptible pathogens for over 24 hours.

claims.text: CI: only known hypersensitivity to it.
claims.quote: There are no significant contraindications to its use other than known hypersensitivity to fosfomycin or to any component of the formulation.

claims.text: Preg: generally considered safe for cystitis; caution in breastfeed (unknown).
claims.quote: Fosfomycin crosses the placenta but is generally considered to be safe for treatment of cystitis in pregnant women. How much fosfomycin enters breast milk is unknown, and caution is advised if treatment with fosfomycin is necessary for breastfeeding women.
claims.locator: Use of Fosfomycin During Pregnancy and Breastfeeding

claims.text: Caution: well tolerated; mainly GI sx (nausea, diarrhea).
claims.quote: Fosfomycin is generally well-tolerated and has a low rate of adverse effects, which include mainly gastrointestinal symptoms (eg, nausea, diarrhea).
